answer_1.quote: We propose reinforcement learning on a pre-trained large language model (LLM) ... to simplify sentences while preserving desirable attributes for language acquisition.
answer_1.outputs: simplified sentences (text simplifications) aligned with target CEFR levels

answer_2.quote: As automatic metrics for simplicity, we employed LENS and SALSA, which are two recently proposed model-based evaluation methods. For fluency and adequacy, we employed an instruction-tuned language model as an off‑the‑shelf evaluation model.

answer_3.quote: For fluency and adequacy, we employed an instruction‑tuned language model as an off‑the‑shelf evaluation model, which was shown to be effective in automatic translation quality evaluations. We used Llama-3-8b-instruct model as the evaluation model.

answer_4.quote: We performed a human evaluation to assess the simplification quality from human perspectives. We recruited three graduate‑level students majoring in linguistics to perform the evaluation. The evaluators were first trained ... and then given a guideline to evaluate the following aspects of the samples: fluency, simplicity, adequacy, and CEFR sentence level.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators made binary judgments for fluency, simplicity, and adequacy, and judged whether the simplified sentence matches the desired CEFR level ("Level") and if it is preferable compared to another level ("Prefer").
